title: Examining PI3K-signaling-dependent regulation of lens organelle free zone formation via immunolocalization and immunoblotting in chick embryos
protocol: Place 4 100 mm petri dishes in a laminar flow hood under sterile conditions.
Crack eggs one at a time into a 100 mm Petri dish.
Decapitate embryos using sharp Dumont Standard Tip Forceps.
Make an incision along the equator of the eye to allow the lens/vitreous to roll out with minimal damage to the lens.
Pinch off lenses from the vitreous and place them into well plates containing Complete Medium.
Place heads in a dish filled with Tris-Dextrose buffer.
Move one head at a time to another dish filled with Tris-Dextrose buffer.
Cut open the eye along the equator using standard forceps.
Grab the vitreous with standard forceps and remove the lens/vitreous together.
Place the removed lens/vitreous in a dish filled with Complete Medium prewarmed to 37°C.
Under the microscope, place one lens/vitreous on a petri dish lid.
Use forceps to stabilize the vitreous while pinching underneath the lens to detach it from the vitreous.
Transfer each isolated lens immediately to a 48 well plate filled with 0.5 mL Complete Medium per well.
Place each lens in a separate well of the 48 well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C in a humidified tissue culture incubator with 5% CO2 and normoxia for 1 hour.
Incubate lenses for 1 hour.
Remove lenses that develop opacities from the study.
Prepare signaling pathway inhibitors from a stock solution of 10 mM.
Dilute inhibitors in 37°C pre-warmed Complete Medium.
Use DMSO as a control vehicle.
Add diluted inhibitors to the media.
Place the well plate in a 37°C humidified tissue culture incubator with 5% CO2.
Incubate for 24 hours.
Determine the efficacy of inhibitors to block a signaling pathway.
Examine impact on downstream signaling effectors using an immunoblot approach.
Use pan-PI3K inhibitor LY294002 at 100 μM or CH5132799 at 25 μM or 100 μM for PI3K inhibition studies.
Use Akt-specific inhibitor MK-2206 at 10 μM to study PI3K signaling pathways.
Determine efficacy of PI3K inhibitors based on inhibition of Akt activity using immunoblot approach.
Wash lenses twice with PBS in a 48 well plate.
Fix lenses with 0.5 mL/well 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 h at 4°C.
Wash lenses twice with PBS.
Cryoprotect lenses in 0.5 mL/well 30% sucrose in PBS for 24 h at 4°C.
Store lenses in sucrose for up to 1 month if needed.
Prepare lenses for immunolocalization analysis.
Preserve tissue integrity through the next steps.
Conduct immunoblotting protocol.
Perform immunolocalization protocol.
Using a dissecting microscope and standard forceps, microdissect each lens to yield three unique differentiation state specific fractions.
Place a lens on the lid of a 100 mm petri dish.
Remove the lens epithelium first.
Separate the cortical fiber cells from the central, nuclear fiber cells.
Create a shallow puncture in the anterior epithelium, denoted by (E), located at the top of the lens.
Widen the tear in the epithelium and grab along the tear with the tips of the forceps.
Pull away the entire epithelium from the fiber cell mass.
Use forceps to remove the cortical fiber cells (FP) from the central fiber cells (FC).
Place each microdissected region on ice in separate 0.5 mL microfuge tubes containing Imidazole Buffer with protease/phosphatase inhibitors at a 1:100 dilution.
Combine all like fractions together in one tube.
Repeat the microdissection procedure for each lens in the study.
Store samples at -80°C until ready to use if not proceeding immediately to protein extraction.
Add the extraction buffer to each sample in equal volume to the Imidazole Buffer.
Homogenize the tissue using disposable plastic pestles that fit the microfuge tube until tissue pieces are no longer visible, approximately 30 seconds.
Incubate the homogenized tissue on ice for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge the extracted samples for 5 minutes at 15000 x g.
Remove the supernatant carefully and place it in new microfuge tubes.
Dilute epithelial cell samples obtained from 5-10 lenses at a ratio of 1:20 for the protein assay using Imidazole Buffer.
Dilute fiber cell samples obtained from 5-10 lenses at a ratio of 1:80 using Imidazole Buffer.
Generate a standard curve (0.025 mg/mL to 2 mg/mL) using Bovine Serum Albumin protein standards.
Load 5 μL in triplicate for each sample and the standard curve in a 96 well plate.
Load a blank sample at 5 μL in triplicate, which is Imidazole Buffer.
Mix reagents A and B in a 50:1 ratio and add 200 μL of this solution to each well.
Cover and incubate the plate for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Measure the absorbance at 562nm on a SpectraMax 360 plate reader.
Remove lenses from the sucrose cryoprotectant using forceps.
Embed lenses in about 4 mL tissue freezing media in a (22 × 22mm) square mold.
Position lenses under a dissecting scope so that the equatorial region is facing up.
Place the mold with embedded lenses into a dry ice/ethanol bath to freeze the lenses.
Embed lenses on the chuck and sections are cut using the cryostat set to -25°C.
Place frozen blocks inside the cryostat for a minimum of 20 minutes before sectioning to allow tissue to acclimate.
Pick up frozen sections on a microscope slide by touching the slide to the tissue.
Using a hydrophobic pen, draw a square around each section.
Add 100 μL Permeabilization Buffer to the square created with the hydrophobic pen.
Incubate for 30 min at approximately 22°C.
Remove the Permeabilization Buffer.
Incubate sections in 100 μL Block Buffer at approximately 22°C for 1 hour.
Remove Block Buffer.
Incubate sections in primary antibodies diluted in Block Buffer at either 37°C for 3 hours or 4°C for approximately 16 hours.
Remove primary antibody and wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes three times.
Incubate with appropriate secondary antibody diluted in the Block Buffer containing DAPI (1:1000) at 37°C for 2 hours.
Remove secondary antibody and wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes three times.
Add a drop of ProLong Diamond Antifade mounting media.
Cover with a Microscope Cover Glass coverslip.
Acclimate the frozen sections to 22°C for about 10 minutes before beginning the immunolocalization protocol.
Optimize incubation times for some primary antibodies if necessary.
Prepare samples to be loaded and run.
For each well on a WES, include your sample, 0.6 μL of Fluorescent Master Mix, and bring the volume up to 3 μL with sample buffer diluted to 0.1X from a 10X stock.
Heat prepared samples at 100°C for 5 minutes.
Load 5 μL of biotinylated ladder into the first well of the first row.
Load 3 μL of each prepared sample into the rest of the first row wells.
Load Antibody Diluent II at 10 μL per well into the second row of the plate.
Load Antibody Diluent II into the first well of the third row.
Dilute primary antibodies in Antibody Diluent II to an optimized concentration.
Load 10 μL/well across the third row for the ladder.
Load 10 μL Streptavidin HRP into the first well of the fourth row.
Load 10 μL of secondary antibody into the remainder of the wells across the fourth row.
Mix luminol and peroxide in a 1:1 ratio.
Add 15 μL of the mixed solution to all wells in the fifth row.
Cover the plate with the supplied lid.
Centrifuge at 1000 x g for 5 min.
Load 500 μL of wash buffer into all the wells of the seventh, eighth, and ninth rows.
Remove the seal from the lower part of the plate just prior to running.
Load the plate and a set of capillaries into the WES machine.
Label a plate template with the contents of each well using Bio-Techne’s Compass software.
Prepare samples for electrophoresis using Novex Tris-Glycine 10 well gels.
Add an equal volume of 2X Sample Buffer to the sample, not exceeding 40 μL per well after mixing.
Heat samples for 10 min at 100°C after adding 2x Sample Buffer.
Choose pre-made polyacrylamide gradient gels depending on protein molecular weights.
Wash the wells in each lane three times with 1x Running buffer, leaving running buffer in at the last wash step.
Place gel in an XCell SureLock Mini-Cell Electrophoresis apparatus.
Fill middle of apparatus with 1x Running buffer.
Connect to power source and run at 80 V until bands run through stacking gel.
Increase voltage up to 120 V when bands reach the stacking gel.
Stop electrophoresis when the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Transfer protein bands from the gel to a PVDF membrane (4 h).
Cut the PVDF membrane to fit the size of the gel (8 cm × 8 cm).
Hydrate the PVDF membrane in 100% methanol for 10 s and then wash with milliQ water.
Place a foam sponge on a cassette from a Hoefer TE22 Mini Tank Blotting Unit, followed by a piece of chromatography paper.
Place the polyacrylamide gel on top of the chromatography paper.
Place the PVDF membrane on top of the gel.
Add another piece of chromatography paper and another sponge over the PVDF membrane.
Close the cassette and place it in the transfer apparatus.
Fill the apparatus with 1x Transfer buffer between min and max lines.
Connect to a power source and start the transfer at 280 mA for 210 minutes.
Remove the PVDF membrane from the cassette after transfer is complete.
Place the PVDF membrane in 5% milk (prepared by mixing 10 g of powdered milk with 200 mL of 1X TBS-T, pH adjusted to 7.6) for 1 hour at 22°C on a gentle rocking apparatus.
Pour out the 5% milk solution and add primary antibodies diluted in 5% milk.
Rock the mixture approximately 16 hours at 4°C.
Identify the lens section under low magnification (5X or 10X) using an LSM800 Zeiss Confocal Microscope.
Switch to 40X magnification for detailed examination.
Adjust the optical section thickness based on the area of interest.
Acquire a z-stack if the entire thickness of the section is required.
Adjust the laser wavelength and detector gain until staining intensity is bright/clear without over saturating.
Decrease the laser wavelength if the range indicator shows over saturation.
Set up a tile in Zeiss’ confocal software (Zen) that extends across the entire lens section.
Acquire the image using the tile application.
Use Zen software to adjust brightness/contrast of images.
Overlay specific channels using Zen software.
Measure staining intensity with Zen software.
Create orthogonal projections using Zen software.
Acquire an image using an optical section thickness of 0.7 μm.
Wash the PVDF membrane with TBS-T for 30 minutes at 22°C.
Incubate the membrane in secondary antibody tagged with HRP diluted in 5% milk for 2 hours at 22°C.
Wash the PVDF membrane with TBS-T for 30 minutes at 22°C.
Incubate the membrane in ECL plus for 5 minutes.
Detect bands using a FluorChem E&M imager.
